title: Adaptive league native policy-head pilot
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Updating the native postflop policy head under a stricter source-policy trust region will produce broader, externally relevant learned action changes than sparse zero residual adapters, while preserving the frozen separate preflop head.
material_change: Resume Standard10; reset optimizer/hand counter; train only policy_head and value_head with postflop PPO, source KL 1, target KL 0.01, advantage clip 3, lr 3e-5; same adaptive three-opponent league and 25% self-play; no position adapters.
baseline: Adapter-only predecessor completed 263608 production hands and passed selected internal mirrors but failed fresh Slumbot 5000 at -53.86 bb/100 CI95 [-92.75,-14.97]. Active Standard10 external baseline is -11.4275 bb/100.

result.summary: Native postflop policy-head league training completed 263464 production hands with stable trust-region metrics. Iter48 maximized direction-consistent three-anchor discovery mean, but untouched confirmation had negative lower bounds versus Standard10 and corrected CFR96, so no external Slumbot run was launched.
result.conclusion: Broader native postflop-head credit consistently beat the Slumbot-free anchor and had positive point estimates against all three anchors at later checkpoints, but evidence was not robust across Standard10 and CFR96. Freezing the separate preflop head also leaves a major action axis untouched.
result.next_step: Add a narrowly scoped all-policy-heads-only training mode so both separate preflop and postflop heads learn from all streets under exact-source KL, while the representation remains frozen; smoke-test tensor scope before any scale.
